_doc: Allowlist of the N+1 checks (tests/test_no_n_plus_one.py, tests/test_no_n_plus_one_jobs.py, scripts/find_query_loops.py). Every entry needs a written reason; nothing here may hide a real N+1. skip_routes: GET routes the crawler does not measure (file downloads, static, health, external proxies). unreachable_routes: GET routes that answer 200 for no role of the seeded world (redirects to measured pages, one-time tokens), with the reason - a route that answers 200 for nobody and is not listed fails the crawl, and an entry whose route IS measured fails too. route_growth: '<route> [<role>]' (or '<route>' for every role) -> {max_extra, reason}: bounded extra statements allowed on the large world. job_growth: '<case name>' -> {per_row, shapes, reason}: background work that is per row BY DESIGN - at most per_row statements per extra row, and only statements whose normalised SQL starts with one of 'shapes' may repeat per row. jobs_not_batched: @periodic / @job_handler names that handle one entity (not a batch), with the reason. loops: scanner fingerprints '<file>::<function>::<call start>' -> {reason, fn_sha}: loops that are not N+1s (chunk loops, retries, fixed small lists, start-up DDL), pinned to the reviewed code (fn_sha: the function, the module helpers it calls and the module constants they read) - when that code changes the entry must be reviewed again and re-pinned with `.venv/bin/python scripts/find_query_loops.py --refresh <fingerprint>`; entries matching no loop fail.

governance_orders: open orders of a susp.reason: per order by design (app/services/governance.py _orders_job): each open order is closed through the shop's own cancellation (its row locks, the gateway refund, the restock, the REFUND ledger row, the buyer's notice - shop_payments.platform_close_order -> cancel_order) in its own short transaction, so a gateway refund is never rolled back with another order's failure; keyset-picked, at most JOB_BATCH (100) per run within JOB_BUDGET_S, then the job re-queues itself for the rest

governance_refunds: memberships of a sus.reason: per membership by design (app/services/governance.py _refunds_job): each pro-rata refund is its own payment-gateway call and its own short transaction - money moved at the gateway is never rolled back with another member's failure; the next membership is picked by keyset, at most JOB_BATCH (100) per run within JOB_BUDGET_S, then the job re-queues itself for the rest

payroll_monthly_generation: gyms.reason: one short transaction per gym by design: a gym's month (its staff, covered ranges, the multi-row statement INSERT, the explanation jobs, the owner's notification) commits or rolls back on its own and is never held open with another gym's; gyms are picked in keyset chunks of GEN_GYM_BATCH and the work inside one gym is constant whatever its staff count (measured by 'payroll_monthly_generation: staff of one gym')

purge_deleted_accounts: gym owners.reason: one transaction per gym OWNER by design (app/services/accounts.py purge_due_accounts): their whole gyms cascade with them (branches, staff, members' records, files), so one owner's purge never shares a transaction - or a rollback - with another's, and its stored files are deleted only after it commits; inside it the work is set-based (one statement per kind of row / file, whatever the gyms' size). Ordinary accounts are purged a whole chunk per transaction (measured by 'purge_deleted_accounts'); owners are rare (an owner can delete the account only once the gyms have no live memberships, unpaid salaries or active staff)

shop_expire_unpaid.reason: per order by design: every unpaid order is a payment-gateway (Cashfree) order that is verified with the gateway BEFORE its own short transaction (lock the order, cancel it) - no transaction ever waits on an HTTP call; the candidates are read in keyset chunks of 50 and a run stops after EXPIRE_BUDGET_S (app/services/shop_payments.py expire_unpaid_orders)
